source_text: οὐ γὰρ ἐκοίησεν ὁ θεὸς κακόν, οὐδέ ἐστιν τὸ σύνολον ὅλως ἐκ παντὸς εἰς τὸ παράπαν αἵτιος κακοῦ· ἀλλὰ πᾶν ὅπερ ἂν αὐτεξούσιον οὕτως ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ γεγονὸς ᾖ πρὸς τὸ φυλάξασθαι καὶ τηρῆσαι νόμον, ὃν αὐτὸς δικαὶως διεστείλατο, μὴ τηρῆσαν λέγεται κακόν. βαρυτάτη δὲ βλάβη τὸ παρακοῦσαι θεοῦ, τοὺς ὅρουσ τῆς κατὰ τὸ αὐτεξούσιον ὑπερβάντα δικαιοσύνης. ὅθεν ἐπειδὴ κατερρυπώθη καὶ κατεμάνθη τῆς άποφάσεως 5 ἀποστατήσας ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ κηλῖδας ἐναπεμάξατο πλάνης, »πόνον« κατὰ τὴν γραφὴν συλλαβών, ἵνα τὸν ἄνθρωπον φανταζειν ἀεὶ πρὸς ἀδικίαν ἔχῆ καὶ κινεῖν, ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀθάντρον κακὸν ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς τοῦ διαβόλου ἰδὼν αὐτὸν γεγενημένον, καθάπερ καὶ ὁ διάβολος πλάνος ἦν, τοὺς δερματίνους χιτῶνας διὰ τοῦτο κατεσκεύασεν, οἱονεὶ νεκούτητι <τινὶ> περιβαλὼν αὐτόν, ὅπως διὰ τῆς λύσεως τοῦ σώματος πᾶν τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ γεννηθὲν κακὸν Προηπόρηται δὲ ἤδη καὶ ἀπεδείχθη τοὺς δερματίνους χιτῶνας μὴ εἶναι τὰ σώματα. ὅμως δὲ καὶ πάλιν (οὐ γὰρ ἅπαξ ῥητέον) φράζωμεν. αὐτὸς πρὸ τῆς κατασκευῆς αὐτῶν ὁ πρωτόπλαστος ὁμολογεῖ καὶ ὀστᾶ ἔχειν καὶ σάρκας, ὁπότε δὴ τὴν γυναῖκα προσενεγθεῖσαν σὐτῶ θεασάμενος »τοῦτο νῦν ὀστοῦν« ἰφώνησεν »ἐκ τῶν ὀστῶν μου καὶ σᾶρξ ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου· αὕτη κληθήσεται γυνή, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς ἐλήφθη. ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείφει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ και τὴν μητέρα, καὶ προσκολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν«. οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἀνέξομαι φληναφώντων τινῶν καὶ βιαζομένων ἀπηρυθριασμένως τὴν γραφήν, ἵνααὐτοίς δὴ σαρκὸς μὴ εἶναι προχωρήσῃ ἡ ἀνάστασις, ὀστᾶ νοητὰ καὶ σάρκας ὑποτιθεμένων, καὶ ἄλλοτε ἄλλως ἄνω καὶ κάτω μεταβαλλομένων ἀλληγορίαις, καὶ ταῦτα οὕτως ὼς γέγραπται παραλαμβάνεσθαι κρατύνοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν γραφήν, ἔνθα πυνθανομένοις τοῖς Φαρισαίοις περὶ χωρισμοῦ γυναικὸς ἀποκρίνεται· »οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ὁ κτίσας ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησε; καὶ εἰπεν, ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείωει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα« πῶς γὰρ ἐπὶ ψυχῶν μόνον τό »αὐξάνεσθε <καὶ πληθύνεσθε> καὶ πληρώσατε τὴν γῆν« παραληπτέον, ἢ τό »ἔλαβε χοῦν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἕπλασε τὸν ἄνθρωπονε«, ὅ κυρίως ἐπὶ τοῦσώματος λελέχθαι φαίνεται; οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ χοὸς καὶ τῶν βαρυτέρων τὴν οὐσίαν ἐκτήσατο ἡ ψυχή. ὥστε συνέστηκεν ἐκ παντὸς ἀληθέστατα πρὸ τῶν δερματίνων σεσωματοποιῆσθαι χιτώνων τὸν ἄνθρωπον. ταῦτα γὰρ τοῦ ἐκπεσεῖν αὐτὸν ἅπαντα εἴρηται, τὰ δὲ κατὰτ τοὺς χετῶνας μετὰ τὸ ἐκπεσεῖν. Ὅθεν ἔωμεν πάλιν ἐπισκεψόμενοι τὰ ἐν χερσίν, ἱκανῶς ἀποδείξαντες μὴ εἶναι τοὺς δερμαντίνους χιτῶνας τὰ σώματα, ἀλλὰ τῆν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀλόγου τῶν ζῴων νεκρότητα κατεσκευασμένην· τοῦτο γὰρλείπεται. ἀμέλει τῶν ὅρων ἔξω τοῦ παραδείσου κατὰ ταύτην ἐξοικίζεται τὴν αἰτίαν· οὐ γάρ, ὅτι μὴ θέλων ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου δρέψασθαι τῆς ζωῆς αὐτὸν καὶ φαγεῖν ἐξέβαλεν (ἐδύνατο γὰρ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ζῆ, αὐθις φαγὼν ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς), ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα μὴ ἀθάνατον, ὡς ὑπεθέμεθα, γενηθῇ τὸ κακόν. ἐπεὶ διὰ τί τὸν Χριστὸν ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀπέστελλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν, εἰ ὅλως ἤθελε ζωῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἄγευστον ἀποθανεῖν εἰς τὸ παντελές; εἰ δὲ ἐκ μεταμέλου φαίη τοῦτο πεποιηκέναι τὸν θεὸν ὁ ἀντικέγων, ἀσθενὴς αὐτῷ ὁ λόγος, μεταγινώσκοντα τ]ν θεὸν εἰσάγων. ἀλλ᾿ οὔτε ἀσύνετος τοῦ μέλλοντος ὁ θεὸς οὔτε κακοποιός, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄκρως ἀγαθὸς καὶ προγινώσκων τὰ ὥστε οὐκ ἄρα διὰ τὸ μὴ σῴζεσθαι εἰς τὸν αἰ[νωα φαγόντα αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς ἐξέβαλεν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ νεκρωθῆναι πρῶντον θανάτῳ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, ἵν᾿ οὕτως μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ἐκτακεἰσης τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἰγερθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος καθαρὸς φάγῃ τῆς ζωῆς. Μηδεὶς δὲ ἀβέλτερος ὢν παρακινδυνευέτω ὡς τούτων ἑτέρως λεχθέντων. ὁ γὰρ ὅλως ὁριζόμενος τὴν σάρκα μὴ εἶναι ταύτηνἀθανασίας δεκτικήν, ὄντως ἀνοίας ὑπεύθυνος ὢν νόσῳ βλασφημεῖ. διὰ τί γὰρ μετὰ τὴν τῶν χιτώνων τῶν δερματίνων ὁ Ἀδὰμ κατασκευὴν ἐκβάλλεται, κωλυόμενος φαγεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ζῆσαι, εἰ ὅλως ἀδύνατον ἦν μετὰ σώματος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ζῆσαι τὸν ἄνθρωπον; ὡς δυναμένου γὰρ αὐτοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἐὰν ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς γεύσηται λαβών, ἡ κώλυσις γίγνεται. φησὶ γάρ· »καὶ ἐποίησε κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀδὰμ καὶ τῆ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ χιτ[νας δερματίνους καὶ ἐνέδυσεν αὐτούς. καὶ εἶεν ὁ θεός· ἰδού, γέγονεν Ἀδὰμ ὡς εἶς ἐξ ἡμῶν, τοῦ γινώσκειν καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν· καὶ νῦν μή ποτε ἐκτείνῃ τὴν χεῖρα καὶ λάβῃ τοῦ ζήλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ καὶ φάηῃ καὶ ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. καὶ ἐξαπέσταειλεν ἀυτὸν κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τοῦ παραδείσου τῆς τρυφῆς ἐργάζεσθαι τὴν γῆυν, ἐξ ἧς ἐλήφθη, καὶ ἐξέβαλε τὸν Ἀδάμ«. ἐσύνατο ζῆν εἰς τὸν αἰ[να τὸ σῶμα καὶ ἀθάνατον ἔσεσθαι, εἰ μὴ κεκώλυτο γεύσασθαι τῆς ζωῆς. ἐκωλύθη δέ, ὅπως ἡ μὲν ἁμαρτίαν συναποκτανθεῖσα τῷ σώματι θάνῃ, τὸ δὲ σῶμα ἀνασταθῇ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἵνα τοίνυν μὴ ᾖ κακὸν ἀθάνατον ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὡς ἔφην, ἣ ἀείζῳον, ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν κρατιεύουσαν, ἅτε ἐν ἀθανάτῳ βλαστήσασαν σώματι καὶ ἀθάνατον ἔχουσαν τὴν τροφήν, ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν διὰ τοῦτο θνητὸν ἀπεφήνατο νεκρότητι περιβαλών. τοῦτο γὰρ οἱ δερμάτινοι χιτῶνες ἐβούλοντο, ἵνα δὴ διὰ τῆς λύσεως τοῦ σώματος καὶ τῆς διαιρέσεως ἡ ἁμαρτία κάτωθεν αὐτόπεεμνος πᾶσα διαφθαρῇ, ὡς μηδὲ κἂν βραχύτατον ῥίζης ἐαθῆναι μέρος, ἀφ᾿ οὗ νέαι βλάσται πάλιν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀναβήσονται.
pass_a_gloss: For God did not make evil, nor is the whole responsible for evil in any way; but everything that is self-determined has come into being by Him for the purpose of keeping and observing the law, which He Himself justly ordained, and not keeping it is called evil. The greatest harm is disobeying God, those who transgress the boundaries of righteousness according to self-determination. From which, since man was corrupted and defiled by the rejection of the statement of God and was stained with the spots of error, 'he received toil' according to Scripture, so that he would always be inclined towards injustice and be moved, God, the Almighty, seeing him become immortal evil through the plotting of the devil, just as the devil was a deceiver, made the skin garments for this reason, as if wrapping him in a kind of necrosis, so that through the dissolution of the body all the evil born in him might be destroyed. It has already been stated and demonstrated that the skin garments are not the bodies. Nevertheless, let us say again, for it is not to be said only once, the first-formed man confesses that he has bones and flesh, when, seeing the woman brought to him, he said 'this now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken from her man.' On account of this, a man leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife, and the two become one flesh. I will not endure those who are deceitful and violently force the Scripture, so that the resurrection may not seem to be of the flesh, hypothesizing intelligible bones and flesh, and changing allegories in various ways, and taking these as if they were written, with Christ confirming the Scripture, where, when the Pharisees ask about divorce, He answers, 'Have you not read that He who created from the beginning made male and female? And He said, for this reason a man shall leave his father and mother.' How can 'be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth' be understood as referring only to souls, or 'the Lord God took dust from the earth and formed man'? This seems to be said primarily of the body, for the soul did not acquire its substance from dust and heavier things. So, it has been established most truly that before the skin garments man was formed from all things. These things were said so that he might fall, but the things concerning the garments are after the fall. Therefore, let us examine again, having sufficiently demonstrated that the skin garments are not the bodies, but the mortality created from the irrationality of animals; this remains. Without a doubt, those outside the boundaries of paradise are settled according to this cause; for it is not that God, not wanting him to eat from the tree of life and live, expelled him, for He was able to live forever, eating again from the tree of life, but so that evil might not become immortal. Since, why did God send Christ from heaven to earth, if He wanted man to die without tasting life at all? If the one who contradicts seems to say that God did this out of regret, his argument is weak, introducing a God who repents. But God is neither ignorant of the future nor evil, but also supremely good and foreknowing, so that He did not expel him because he would not be saved to eternal life after eating from the tree of life, but so that sin might die first by death, and then, after sin has been destroyed, man might rise and eat the life. Let no one, being reckless, dare to say that these things were said differently. For the one who defines flesh as not being capable of immortality is truly responsible for foolishness, being sick with blasphemy. Why, after the creation of the skin garments, was Adam expelled, being prevented from eating from the tree of life and living, if it were impossible for man to live forever with a body? For if he were able not to die, having tasted the life, the prevention would be in vain. For it is said, 'And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife skin garments and clothed them. And God said, behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take of the tree of life and eat and live forever.' And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure to work the earth from which he was taken, and He expelled Adam.' The body was able to live forever and become immortal, if it had not been prevented from tasting the life. But it was prevented, so that sin might die together with the body, and the body might rise again, sin having been destroyed, so that man might eat the life. Therefore, God declared him mortal, wrapping him in death, so that man might not be immortal evil, as I said, or always living, having sin reigning in him, as if sin had sprouted in an immortal body and had immortal nourishment. For this is what the skin garments meant, so that through the dissolution of the body and its separation, all sin might be destroyed below, so that not even a small part of the root might be left, from which new shoots of sins might arise again.

pass_b_english: God did not create evil, nor is the sum of things in any way responsible for evil. Rather, everything that possesses self-determination came into being through Him for the purpose of keeping and observing the law that He Himself justly ordained; failing to keep it is what is called evil. The greatest harm is disobeying God — transgressing the boundaries of righteousness that belong to self-determination. Because humanity was corrupted and defiled by rejecting God’s command and stained with the spots of error, “he received toil” according to Scripture (Genesis 3:17-19), so that he would always be inclined toward injustice and driven toward it. God the Almighty saw that man had become an immortal evil through the devil’s plotting — just as the devil himself was a deceiver — and for this reason He made the skin garments, wrapping him, as it were, in a kind of necrosis, so that through the dissolution of the body all the evil born in him might be destroyed. It has already been stated and demonstrated that the skin garments are not the bodies themselves. Nevertheless, let us say it again, for it cannot be said only once: the first-formed man confessed that he had bones and flesh even before the garments were made. When the woman was brought to him and he saw her, he exclaimed, “This now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken from her man” (Genesis 2:23). “For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). I will not tolerate those who deceitfully and violently force Scripture, so that the resurrection may not be seen as a resurrection of the flesh. They hypothesize “intelligible bones and flesh,” shifting allegories in various directions, and treat these inventions as if they were written, even though Christ Himself confirms Scripture. When the Pharisees questioned Him about divorce, He answered, “Have you not read that He who created from the beginning made them male and female? And He said, ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother’” (Matthew 19:4–5). How can “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth” (Genesis 1:28) be understood as referring only to souls? Or “The Lord God took dust from the earth and formed the man” (Genesis 2:7)? This is said primarily of the body, for the soul did not acquire its substance from dust and heavier elements. Therefore it is most truly established that before the skin garments, man was fully embodied. The earlier statements were made so that he might fall; the statements about the garments come after the fall. Let us examine the matter again, having sufficiently demonstrated that the skin garments are not the bodies, but the mortality fashioned from the irrationality of animals — this is what remains. Beyond question, those outside the boundaries of paradise are settled there for this very reason. It was not because God, unwilling for him to eat from the tree of life and live, expelled him; God was able to let him live forever, eating again from the tree of life. Rather, it was so that evil might not become immortal. Why else would God have sent Christ from heaven to earth, if He had wanted man to die without ever tasting life? If the opponent claims God did this out of regret, his argument is weak, introducing a God who repents. But God is neither ignorant of the future nor evil; He is supremely good and foreknowing. So He did not expel man because man would not be saved to eternal life by eating from the tree of life, but so that sin might die first through death, and then, after sin has been destroyed, man might rise and eat of life. Let no reckless person dare to say these things were spoken differently. The one who defines flesh as incapable of immortality is truly guilty of foolishness, diseased with blasphemy. Why, after the creation of the skin garments, was Adam expelled and prevented from eating from the tree of life and living, if it were impossible for man to live forever with a body? For if he had been able not to die by tasting of life, the prevention would have been pointless. Scripture says, “And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife skin garments and clothed them. And God said, ‘Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take of the tree of life and eat and live forever.’ And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure to work the earth from which he was taken, and He expelled Adam” (Genesis 3:21–24). The body was able to live forever and become immortal, if it had not been prevented from tasting life. But it was prevented, so that sin might die together with the body, and the body might rise again with sin destroyed, so that man might eat of life. Therefore God declared him mortal, wrapping him in death, so that man might not be an immortal evil — as I said — or an ever-living one, with sin reigning in him, as if sin had sprouted in an immortal body and had immortal nourishment. This is what the skin garments intended: that through the dissolution of the body and its separation, all sin might be destroyed from below, so that not even the smallest part of a root might remain, from which new shoots of sins might arise again.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the nature of the skin garments versus the original body, the purpose of Adam's mortality, and the distinction between sin and the body. All scripture citations in Pass B (Genesis 3:17-19, Genesis 2:23, Genesis 2:24, Matthew 19:4-5, Genesis 1:28, Genesis 2:7, Genesis 3:21-24) correctly identify the Greek allusions and quotations. Pass A and B are consistent with the Greek source.
